results.content: K E Y W O R D S card-based design tool, design activities configuration, design representation, design research, design science research 1 | INTRODUCTION Information Systems (IS) design research leverages innovation by designing solutions based on digital technologies (Hevner & Gregor, 2020; Nambisan et al., 2017). Category Examples of evidence Implication for this article Configuring design research • Diversity of design research (Rai, 2017), design research project options (Smuts et al., 2022) • Deficits in the application of design concepts/methods (Cahenzli & Winter, 2023) • Challenge of operationalising guidelines (Cater-Steel et al., 2019; Winter & vom Brocke, 2021) • One-size fits all approaches • Idealised processes (Parnas & Clements, 1986) • Need for awareness of specific options, steps • Need for detailed how-to instructions • Account for methodical diversity • Ensure adaptability Representing design research • Limited guidance on how to communicate with stakeholders (Cahenzli & Winter, 2023) • Deficits of how communication accounts for design peculiarities (Cahenzli, 2022) • Difficulties in summarising large projects; “Faking design rationality” (Parnas & Clements, 1986) • Need for faithful representations • Need for guidance on how to convey design research Interpreting/ implementing design research (viewer) • Multi-stakeholders, such as people who face a similar problem, evaluation partners, developers, collaborators (Cahenzli & Winter, 2023) • Heterogeneity of how design processes are reported, room for interpretation • Enable stakeholders to interpret design research • Enable stakeholders to perform design research (processes) FIGURE 1 Design creation versus design view.

results.content: P283 MORAL DISTRESS IN ONCOLOGY NURSING, A CROSS SECTIONAL STUDY OF NURSES IN A COMPREHENSIVE CANCER CENTER Pamela McLaughlin, MSN, RN, OCN®, Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center, Buffalo, NY; Melissa Hiscock, BSN, RN, CWOCN®, OCN®, CPPS, Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center, Buffalo, NY Research Oncology nursing care frequently involves a delicate balance between aggressive therapies and the patient’s quality of life. Further study is required to be deeply understand the experience of colorectal survivors’ adaptation and transition to their life after cancer treatment and develop arbitration plan for im-proving the colorectal cancer survivors’ quality of life P302 COUPLES’ EXPERIENCE OF UNCERTAINTY IN FACING GYNECOLOGICAL CANCER Yingzi Zhang, PhD, RN, University of Rochester, Roch-ester, NY; Sally Norton, PhD, RN, FNAP, FPCN, FAAN, University of Rochester, Rochester, NY; Marie Flannery, PhD, RN, AOCN®, University of Rochester School of Nursing, Rochester, NY; Rachel Carter, MS, University of Rochester, Rochester, NY; Charles Kamen, PhD, MPH, University of Rochester, Rochester, NY Research Uncertainty is common and distressing for patients and their partners, which causes clinically significant levels of depression and anxiety.
